governance_posts.description:
Greetings, Aave community!

Aave Labs has continued to make steady progress on multiple protocol endeavors in line with its service provider scope.

The below summary highlights developments in the Aave Protocol and reflects Aave Labs’ transparent and collaborative approach of building in public, welcoming community feedback, and fostering auditability through open-source principles.

July update:

  • Launched Aave V4 on Avalanche and completed preparation for the Maple syrupUSDG Spoke on Ethereum, with its AIP created for execution on August 1st.
  • Published Certora’s formal verification reports for Aave V4.
  • Launched Aave V3 on Monad and onboarded stcUSD to Aave V3 MegaETH.
  • Advanced portfolio discipline, deprecating legacy V3 reserves, matured Pendle PTs, and oracle feeds for rarely used assets.
  • Updated Aave V3 LTV and E-Mode parameters in support of LlamaRisk.
  • Deployed the Remote GSM on Arbitrum and launched GHO in Monad.
  • Launched Stable Vaults as a core component of the Aave App and the Aave Kit.
  • Passed the Aave App Launch ARFC and advanced Android features.
  • Grew Aave Horizon deposits and launched its public maintenance thread.
  • Advanced Aave Pro and Aave Interface improvements, including gasless voting.

Aave Protocol

Security remained a central focus throughout the month, with continued engagement from the internal security team and Aave Labs’ security partners.

Aave V4

Aave V4 crossed $325M in deposits during July, another all-time high, with deposits nearly doubling over the month. Aave V4 also went live on Avalanche in July, marking its first expansion across multiple chains beyond Ethereum. The team also completed preparation work for the Maple syrupUSDG Spoke on Ethereum during the month, with the corresponding AIP created for execution on August 1st.

On the security side, Certora published its formal verification reports for Aave V4. The reports reflect the ongoing security effort carried out throughout the protocol’s development, which produces a formal list of properties against which the code is verified, providing mathematical assurance that the code behaves as intended under the modeled conditions and extending the assurance layer beyond audits.

Implementation of the Risk Steward for Aave V4 also progressed toward activation. The Risk Steward lets a Risk Council apply frequent, routine risk-parameter adjustments within bounds set by governance, without requiring a full governance vote each time, following the same model established by the Aave V3 Risk Steward. Related to this effort, and in support of @LlamaRisk, the team also implemented regular supply and borrow cap increases on Aave V4, aimed at keeping capacity aligned with market growth.

The team is working closely with the Babylon team on the Bitcoin vaults integration (Babylon TBV) proposed in this temp check, executing the design, integration, and audit reviews of Babylon’s implementation. The integration brings a new use case for BTC within the Aave Protocol, letting native Bitcoin serve as collateral without wrapping, bridging, or custodians.

Aave V3

Aave V3 launched on Monad, one of the EVM networks with the highest throughput. Following the technical assessment published previously, stcUSD was also onboarded to Aave V3 MegaETH.

In support of @LlamaRisk, an Aave V3 LTV and E-Mode update was executed, reducing loan-to-value ratios to zero for a small set of assets with low liquidity across several markets, introducing a new stablecoin eMode category on Mantle, and raising wstETH borrow caps on Ethereum Core and Prime.

The team also worked closely with @LlamaRisk on a portfolio discipline effort. In July, two governance proposals went live applying the Aave Risk Framework at portfolio level, deprecating V3 reserves with minimal activity and matured Pendle principal tokens (representing approximately $85M supplied), and retiring oracle feeds for rarely used assets across V2 and V3 where continued maintenance is no longer justified. Core stablecoin and bluechip markets are unaffected: the deprecated positions are wound down gradually, and no forced action is taken against existing positions.

Governance Proposals

Aave Labs actively supported the DAO’s governance efforts throughout July, bringing AIPs onchain during the month, including the Aave V3 Monad activation and the Aave V3 LTV and E-Mode update. The AIP for the Maple syrupUSDG Spoke onboarding on Ethereum was also created in July, with execution set for August 1st. These proposals, alongside others such as the PAXG onboarding and the Aave App Launch, were shaped through ARFC discussion and Snapshot voting as a collaborative effort with the DAO.

Beyond its own proposals, the team continued to support fellow service providers throughout their proposal efforts. A consolidated view of recent proposal activity is available on the voting dashboard.

Asset Technical Assessments

The team published the technical assessment of PAXG and the technical assessment of syrupUSDG, both on Aave Ethereum. Work is also underway on a number of additional assessments, to be published in the coming weeks.

What else are we working on?

Stable Vaults

In July, Aave Labs introduced Stable Vaults, a backend for embedding stablecoin yield at a fixed rate into any product. The architecture separates an accounting chain, which handles rate management and record-keeping, from earning chains, where deposits are deployed across multiple yield strategies and networks simultaneously. Access is governed through allowlisting, with permissions assigned by role, and each integrating platform configures rates for each user and controls the allocation of revenue generated above the committed rate.

Stable Vaults let businesses accept USDC, USDT, GHO, or their own stablecoin as deposits. Once received, deposits are treated as interchangeable, and withdrawals can be made in any supported stablecoin regardless of the asset originally deposited. Underlying yield strategies route into Aave markets, Savings GHO, or any ERC-4626 compliant vault.

Stable Vaults is a core component of the Aave App and is now part of the Aave Kit. For GHO, the product opens a new distribution channel: businesses that integrate Stable Vaults can route deposits into Savings GHO, extending GHO’s utility and reach beyond direct protocol usage.

GHO

GHO’s backing strength continued to improve, reaching 245% total backing against 601M total supply and $552M total reserves. GHO was also listed on Monad alongside the V3.7 deployment, and a Remote GSM was deployed on Arbitrum, extending the GHO Stability Module (GSM) to a new network. In support of @TokenLogic, 8M GHO were acquired for the Prime instance, expanded the MainnetSwapSteward to swap into GHO, AAVE, and wETH, and granted GHO deployment permissions on Monad. The StkGhoMigrator was also launched, giving stkGHO holders a direct path to migrate into sGHO.

Aave App

The Android app continued advancing toward feature parity with iOS, covering onboarding, trays, animations, and design system alignment. Preliminary testing started for both iOS and Android versions during the month. Separately, the governance proposal formally supporting the Aave App launch passed in July.

Aave Horizon

Aave Horizon continued its growth trajectory, with deposits reaching $358M during the month. In support of @LlamaRisk, the price feeds for RLUSD and USDC on Aave Horizon V3 were updated to price cap adapters (CAPO), aligning with the approach already applied to other assets across the protocol. The team also launched a dedicated, running maintenance thread to consolidate onchain and offchain Aave Horizon updates, including listings, parameter changes, integrations, and operational milestones, in one transparent place.

Aave Pro

Aave Pro shipped a UI update to support Aave V4 usage across chains, letting users view assets, balances, and positions on each of them, timed to the Avalanche launch. ETH and WETH handling was also cleaned up: the two are now combined in the UI, the redundant “convert to WETH” toggle was removed, both balances are shown on the asset page, and WETH was removed from the deposit explore page. Assets can also be grouped by hub or market, with the option to collate them across views.

Aave Interface

The team shipped a governance page refactor, adding a payloads panel to proposals that surfaces payload state, actions, the Seatbelt report, and explorer links. The update corrected timeline timestamps with live countdowns for the next action, added actionable transaction links, and properly handled expired and canceled states.

Gasless voting was also built, replacing the Gelato relay path with Aave’s own relayer for voting. Bug fixes, dependency upgrades, and UI improvements to guide users to try Aave V4 were also rolled out during this month.

Aave Kit

The SDK was improved to support overriding token names, Hubs, and Spokes in a local instance. The team also added support for custom headers, enabling more use cases where they are required for custom instances.

What’s coming next?

Our main focus for the coming month will be:

  • Execute the Maple syrupUSDG Spoke onboarding.
  • Advance the Babylon TBV integration with the Babylon team.
  • Advance Aave App launch preparations following passage of the Launch ARFC.
  • Continue supporting GHO growth, including adoption of Stable Vaults.
  • Continue Aave Pro and Aave Interface improvements.
  • Implement leverage support in Aave Pro.
  • Implement position swaps (collateral swap, debt swap, and repay with collateral) in Aave Pro.

Stay tuned for next month’s update.

Aave Labs

governance_posts.title: Risk Stewards: Supply and Borrow Cap Increases on Aave V3 / 2026.08.11
governance_posts.description:
Summary

LlamaRisk recommends the following parameter changes based on user behavior, on-chain liquidity, and position health observed in the latest review of Aave V3 reserves.

Aave V3 Monad:

  • Increase supply cap for USDC from 150,000,000 to 250,000,000.
  • Increase borrow cap for USDC from 135,000,000 to 225,000,000.
  • Increase supply cap for GHO from 20,000,000 to 40,000,000.
  • Increase borrow cap for GHO from 18,000,000 to 36,000,000.
  • Increase supply cap for USDe from 80,000,000 to 100,000,000.

Aave V3 Core:

  • Increase supply cap for BTC.b from 160 to 225.

USDC (Aave V3 Monad)

USDC has reached 93.0% supply cap utilization (139,428,304 / 150,000,000) and 92.8% borrow cap utilization (125,340,712 / 135,000,000) on the Aave V3 Monad instance.

Supply Distribution


Source: LlamaRisk, August 11, 2026

The top USDC suppliers hold the asset predominantly on a spot basis, with seventeen of the twenty carrying no offsetting debt and the levered remainder running health factors between 1.01 and 1.07. Those carrying debt borrow USDe against USDC collateral, meaning both legs of the position are dollar-denominated. Since USDe is priced at par with USDT, the health factor consequently tracks the USDT peg.

Borrow Distribution


Source: LlamaRisk, August 11, 2026

The top USDC borrowers all carry outstanding debt, with health factors between 1.01 and 1.14 and a median of 1.02. Collateral is posted in syrupUSDC and USDe against USDC and USDT0 debt, so the cohort is dollar denominated on both legs and health factor stability tracks those collateral assets holding their peg.

Recommendation

We recommend raising the supply cap from 150,000,000 to 250,000,000 and the borrow cap from 135,000,000 to 225,000,000 on Aave V3 Monad. Both legs stand above 92% utilization and supply has grown approximately 30% over the past eight days, with the proposed caps landing at approximately 55.8% and 55.7% post-change utilization respectively.

GHO (Aave V3 Monad)

GHO has reached 93.0% supply cap utilization (18,605,503 / 20,000,000) and 75.0% borrow cap utilization (13,508,857 / 18,000,000) on the Aave V3 Monad instance.

Supply Distribution


Source: LlamaRisk, August 11, 2026

The top GHO suppliers hold the asset almost entirely on a spot basis, with 18 of the 19 carrying no offsetting debt and the single levered position running a health factor of 1.11. Supply-side positions therefore carry negligible liquidation exposure, and health factor risk in this reserve sits on the borrow side.

Borrow Distribution


Source: LlamaRisk, August 11, 2026

The top GHO borrowers all carry outstanding debt, with health factors between 1.01 and 1.45 and a median of 1.03. Collateral is led by syrupUSDC and USDe against GHO debt, so the cohort holds dollar denominated collateral against dollar denominated borrowings and health factor stability tracks those collateral assets holding their peg.

Recommendation

We recommend raising the supply cap from 20,000,000 to 40,000,000 and the borrow cap from 18,000,000 to 36,000,000 on Aave V3 Monad. Supply cap utilization stands at 93.0% with supply up approximately 61% over the past eight days, and borrow cap utilization stands at 75.0%, with the proposed caps landing at approximately 46.5% and 37.5% post-change utilization respectively.

USDe (Aave V3 Monad)

USDe has reached 100.0% supply cap utilization (80,001,774 / 80,000,000) on the Aave V3 Monad instance.

Supply Distribution


Source: LlamaRisk, August 11, 2026

The top USDe suppliers run health factors between 1.01 and 2.48 with a median of 1.02, and nineteen of the twenty carry outstanding debt. Borrowing is denominated in USDT0 and USDC against USDe collateral held in the stablecoin E-Mode category at LTV 90.0% and LT 92.0%, so health factor stability tracks the USDT peg, because USDe is priced on par with USDT.

Recommendation

We recommend raising the supply cap from 80,000,000 to 100,000,000 on Aave V3 Monad. The reserve is at its current ceiling, and the proposed cap lands at approximately 80.0% post-change cap utilization while the supplier base borrows stablecoins against USDe collateral. The borrow cap is held unchanged at 36,000,000.

BTC.b (Aave V3 Core)

BTC.b is currently at 38.4% supply cap utilization (61 / 160) on the Aave V3 Core instance.

Supply Distribution


Source: LlamaRisk, August 11, 2026

The top BTC.b suppliers run health factors between 1.13 and 2.21 with a median of 1.46, and eight of the nine carry outstanding debt. Borrowing is denominated entirely in stablecoins and led by USDe, so the cohort holds stablecoin borrowings against BTC.b collateral whose health factor stability tracks the BTC price.

Recommendation

We recommend raising the supply cap from 160 to 225 on Aave V3 Core. The reserve stands at 38.4% supply cap utilization and the proposed cap lands at approximately 27.3% post-change cap utilization.

Specification

Instance Asset Current Supply Cap Recommended Supply Cap Current Borrow Cap Recommended Borrow Cap
Aave V3 Monad USDC 150,000,000 250,000,000 135,000,000 225,000,000
Aave V3 Monad GHO 20,000,000 40,000,000 18,000,000 36,000,000
Aave V3 Monad USDe 80,000,000 100,000,000 36,000,000 -
Aave V3 Core BTC.b 160 225 - -

Next Steps

We will move forward and implement these updates via the Risk Steward process.

Disclosure

This review was independently prepared by LlamaRisk, a DeFi risk service provider funded in part by the Aave DAO. LlamaRisk is not directly affiliated with the protocol(s) reviewed in this assessment and did not receive any compensation from the protocol(s) or their affiliated entities for this work.

The information provided should not be construed as legal, financial, tax, or professional advice.
